stories.headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
stories.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.
stories.why_it_matters: Those advances have been extraordinary. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.
Technical Implementation: For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores.

Deployment & Impact: But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?” Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.

stories.headline: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

stories.headline: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform

stories.headline: Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance
stories.summary: Micron's next-generation 3D NAND, which will enter mass production in 2H 2027, is set to offer three significant advantages: it will double storage density, increase I/O performance by 50% compared to the company's current-generation NAND memory, and decrease power consumption, the company revealed at an event this week. To achieve these aggressive goals, Micron plans to take a page from YMTC's book and adopt wafer-on-wafer bonding.
stories.why_it_matters: Meanwhile, Micron is also developing new materials and denser memory cell architectures to extend 3D NAND scaling beyond G11. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Micron's next-generation 3D NAND, which will enter mass production in 2H 2027, is set to offer three significant advantages: it will double storage density, increase I/O performance by 50% compared to the company's current-generation NAND memory, and decrease power consumption, the company revealed at an event this week.

stories.headline: The Cost of Saying Hello: An Empirical Study of Handshake Overhead in AI Agent Communication Protocols
stories.summary: Skip to main content Search Submit Donate Log in Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence [Submitted on 12 Aug 2026] The Cost of Saying Hello: An Empirical Study of Handshake Overhead in AI Agent Communication Protocols Pranav Varshney Every interaction between AI agents begins with a handshake: the initiating agent must locate its counterpart, learn what it can do, and establish a session before the first useful message can be sent. Surveys of agent communication protocols name handshake overhead as an efficiency criterion, yet none report measurements.
stories.why_it_matters: This paper presents the first empirical, phase-decomposed benchmark of the handshake in three major agent protocols: MCP (in both its 2025 initialize and 2026 discover eras), A2A, and ACP. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: This paper presents the first empirical, phase-decomposed benchmark of the handshake in three major agent protocols: MCP (in both its 2025 initialize and 2026 discover eras), A2A, and ACP.

Technical Implementation: Using each protocol's official SDK, we instrument every request for round trips, per-phase latency, wire bytes, and token cost across cold-start, warm-repeat, capability-mismatch, and degraded-metadata scenarios (N=50 per cell, on loopback and under an emulated 50 ms RTT).

Deployment & Impact: Round trips are not the whole bill: when an LLM reads the counterpart's metadata, handshake cost scales with the counterpart's capability inventory at 24-107 tokens per capability, so a 200-capability counterpart spends 11% of a 200k-token context window before the agent reads its own task.
